description: Cross-language conformance record for the serve hierarchy and service lifecycle. Authority for behavior is docs/contracts/serve-lifecycle.md, section 'Cross-language parity'; this file records which required behaviors each port has shipped. A port that has not implemented serve is PENDING, not FAIL: the harness makes the gap visible without failing a build over work that has not started.

statuses.SHIPPED: the port implements this behavior and has tests pinning it
statuses.PENDING: the port has not implemented this behavior yet; not a failure
statuses.N/A: the behavior is not required of this port, with a reason

constants.description: Values a conforming port MUST reproduce exactly. Unlike the per-language status table below, these do not vary by port.

payload_keys.service: service identifier; never in the topic
payload_keys.error: failure text; never in the topic
payload_keys.address: resolved listen address, on ready_reported only

behaviors.hierarchy: <tool> serve supervises every configured and enabled service; <tool> serve <service> selects exactly one; both share one lifecycle. 2+ positional args is USAGE/2.
behaviors.override_rule: serve <service> starts the service even when services.<name>.enabled is false, provided registration, configuration and policy validate in that order. A disabled service under the supervisor form is skipped silently and does not affect the exit code. Zero resolved services under the supervisor form exits 2.
behaviors.list_flag: the inspection form is the --list flag, not a `list` child.
behaviors.registration_seam: a registry both kit-owned and adopter-owned services register into before the root runs; each registration carries a name, a blocking start, a readiness report and a stop. Duplicate registration fails at construction with an explicit override escape hatch; listing order is registration order.
behaviors.readiness: ready at most once per start; aggregate ready when every started service is ready; a service not ready within ready_timeout is a start failure.
behaviors.lifecycle_events: the six transitions above are surfaced through the bus (under the exact topic strings) or, for a port with no bus, through the log with the same field names.
behaviors.ordered_shutdown: SIGINT/SIGTERM begin a graceful drain and a second signal aborts it; cancel once, then stop in the exact reverse of actual start order, one at a time, each bounded by stop_timeout, all bounded by shutdown_timeout.
behaviors.failure_policy: fail-fast (default) brings every service down on one failure; isolate keeps the rest running.
behaviors.exit_taxonomy: serve outcomes route onto the shared exit-code taxonomy, including a signal stop exiting 0 and TRANSIENT propagating exit 6.
behaviors.config_keys: the services.* key names above are read, with the defaults above. How a port resolves them is not contract.
behaviors.enable_disable_flags: --enable <name> / --disable <name> are repeatable flags on serve that override services.<name>.enabled for one run, under the supervisor form only. --enable on an unconfigured service makes it configured and enabled; --disable on an enabled service skips it silently without affecting the exit code; --enable wins over --disable for the same name. Either flag combined with the selector form is refused as USAGE/2.
behaviors.timeout_flags: --ready-timeout, --stop-timeout and --shutdown-timeout are accepted under both forms, by exactly those names, and override services.<name>.ready_timeout and services.<name>.stop_timeout for every resolved service and services.shutdown_timeout for the run. The duration spelling a port accepts is not contract.

not_required.description: Go-only affordances. A port is not non-conformant for lacking these; see the contract section 'Explicitly not required' for the reasoning on each.

ts.implementation: sdk/ts/src/serve.ts, mounted by registerServe on a commander root

py.implementation: sdk/py/hop_top_kit/serve.py, mounted by register_serve on a Typer root

rs.note: serve::command::mount puts `serve [SERVICE]` with --list, --enable/--disable and the three timeout flags on any clap root, the way the TypeScript port mounts on any commander root; the kit-owned root factory, when it lands, mounts the same command. Arity is refused by resolve() at USAGE/2 rather than by clap so the exit code stays on the shared taxonomy. The one gap left is the env-var spelling (<TOOL>_SERVICES_API_ENABLED): the contract makes it conditional on a port having env resolution, which arrives with the Rust config loader, not with this command.

php.implementation: sdk/experimental/php/src/Serve, mounted as ServeCommand on a Symfony Console application
php.note: The SDK has no event bus, so the lifecycle_events obligation is met through the log sink: the six transitions carry the fixed topic strings and the service/error/address payload keys as structured fields, at INFO for started/ready_reported/stopped and ERROR for failed. Signals need ext/pcntl, which is a builtin on the CI image; availability is probed with function_exists rather than extension_loaded, since disable_functions leaves the extension loaded while blanking every call. Where the pcntl functions are absent the port degrades to the caller-driven stop rather than inventing a different escalation.
